slices.name: alert-dialog
slices.summary: An alert dialog stops you to tell you something you must know before you go on. It has one button, and pressing it says you have read it.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on the action and on Escape. There is no other way out.

props.name: description
props.doc: What happened and what it means for the user. Read out when the dialog opens.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: The one answer, named for what it does: "Sign in again", "Got it", never a bare "OK" when a verb fits.

slices.name: badge
slices.summary: A badge is a small pill that shows a number, such as 3 unread, or a status word, such as Paid. It sits next to the thing it describes.

props.name: status
props.doc: The meaning of the fill. A status badge also needs a word in `children`.

props.name: count
props.doc: A number to show. It caps at `max` and shows "99+".

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest number shown in full. Default 99.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the count counts, such as "unread messages". Read out after the full number.

props.name: children
props.doc: The status word, such as "Overdue".

props.name: decorative
props.doc: Hide the badge from assistive technology because the text beside it already says the same.

slices.name: banner
slices.summary: A banner is a note that stays on the page until the problem is gone or you close it. It tells you something about the page or the system: a trial is ending, a payment failed, a save worked.

props.name: status
props.doc: The kind of message. Shown by an icon and a word, never by colour alone.

props.name: title
props.doc: Optional lead line.

props.name: children
props.doc: The message (children).

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons or links under the message.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Show a close button and call this when it is pressed. The parent removes the banner.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the close button. Required with `onDismiss`.

props.name: urgent
props.doc: Read out at once (`role="alert"`). Use only for an error the user must act on now.

props.name: statusLabel
props.doc: Spoken name of the icon, such as "Error". Defaults to the status word.

slices.name: box
slices.summary: A box is an empty container. You choose how much space goes inside it and between its children, from a fixed list of sizes. It draws nothing until you give it a background.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Pick it for document structure; a Box adds no role.

props.name: padding
props.doc: Padding on all sides, as a space step.

props.name: paddingInline
props.doc: Padding on the inline axis. Wins over `padding`.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.doc: Padding on the block axis. Wins over `padding`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap between children, as a space step. It has an effect only when `display` is "flex" or "grid".

props.name: surface
props.doc: Background, from the surface roles.

slices.name: breadcrumb
slices.summary: A breadcrumb shows the path from the top of the site down to the page you are on, like the trail of crumbs in the fairy tale. Each step back up is a link.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the landmark, such as "Breadcrumb".

props.name: items
props.doc: The path from the root to the current page. The last item is the current page.

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: A router link component, passed to every Link as `as`.

props.name: maxItems
props.doc: More items than this collapse into a "…" button that expands the path.

props.name: expandLabel
props.doc: The accessible name of the "…" button. Pass it in the app's language.

slices.name: button
slices.summary: A button is the thing you press to make something happen. Save, send, delete. If pressing it takes you to another page, it is a link, not a button.

props.name: variant
props.doc: One primary per view region. `subtle` is the quietest: neutral text, no fill or outline until hover. `danger` is only the confirm of a destructive action.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The action is running. The label and the width stay; presses are ignored.

slices.name: card
slices.summary: A card is a bordered box that groups what you know about one thing: a title, some detail, a note at the bottom. The whole card can be one link, or it can just sit there.

props.name: title
props.doc: The card's name. It is the heading, and the link text when the card has an `href`.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The outline level of the title. Pick it for the page's outline, not for the look.

props.name: meta
props.doc: A short, non-interactive line beside the title: a status word, a date.

props.name: children
props.doc: The body.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The footer. With `href` it holds text only: the card is already one link.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the whole card one link named by the title. The link's target covers the card.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Show placeholder lines in the body. The card keeps its size.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.doc: Text for assistive technology while loading.

props.name: empty
props.doc: Body content when there are no children. The caller supplies the empty state.

props.name: error
props.doc: The content failed to load. Replaces the body; announced as an alert.

slices.name: checkbox
slices.summary: A checkbox is a small box you tick to say yes. It is for one independent choice, like accepting the terms, or for picking rows in a list. Ticking one does not untick another.

props.name: label
props.doc: Always visible, and part of the target: a click on it toggles the box.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text, for a box that must be checked. Its presence sets aria-invalid.

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: The mixed state of a parent whose children are partly checked. Cleared when the user toggles it.

slices.name: chip
slices.summary: A chip is a small pill that holds one value the user chose, such as a filter. It can carry a button to remove that value, or it can switch on and off.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `static` shows a value. `removable` adds a remove button. `selectable` is a toggle.

props.name: children
props.doc: The visible text. It stays whole in the accessible name; a long one truncates and a Tooltip shows the rest.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Removable: called when the remove button is pressed.

props.name: removeLabel
props.doc: Removable: the words before the label in the remove button's name. Default "Remove", giving "Remove Status: Shipped".

props.name: selected
props.doc: Selectable: the pressed state, controlled.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.doc: Selectable: the starting state when `selected` is not set.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.doc: Selectable: called with the new state on a press.

slices.name: color
slices.summary: Color tells users what things are for: text, surface, border, the main action. Components ask for a job, never for a shade of blue. Three steps stand between a hex value and a component, so a rebrand or a dark theme changes one step and no component.

slices.name: combobox
slices.summary: A combobox is a text box with a list of suggestions. You type a few letters, the list narrows, and you pick one. Use it when the list is too long to scroll.

props.name: label
props.doc: Always visible.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text. Its presence sets aria-invalid and the error look.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: Shown in the list when the typed text matches nothing. Default "No results".

props.name: loading
props.doc: The options are being fetched. The list says so, and aria-busy is set.

slices.name: confirmation-dialog
slices.summary: A confirmation dialog asks one yes-or-no question before an action goes ahead. You confirm it or cancel it.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on Cancel, Escape and the scrim.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the choice does and what it costs. Read out when the dialog opens.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.doc: Names the action and its object: "Delete 3 files", never "OK".

props.name: destructive
props.doc: The action cannot be undone. The confirm is a danger button and comes first. Focus starts on Cancel, the least destructive choice.

slices.name: critical-confirmation-dialog
slices.summary: A critical confirmation dialog stops the user before an action that cannot be undone and that also removes other things. To go on, the user types the name of the thing they are about to delete.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on Cancel, Escape and the scrim. Ignored while `loading`.

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Called by the confirm button and by Enter, only when the typed value equals `confirmText`.

props.name: description
props.doc: The cost: what goes, how much, and what else goes with it. Read out when the dialog opens.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.doc: Names the action and its object: "Delete project", never "OK".

props.name: confirmText
props.doc: The exact text the user must type. The comparison is exact: case and spaces count.

props.name: fieldLabel
props.doc: The label of the text field: "Type Apollo to confirm".

props.name: fieldDescription
props.doc: Says why the confirm is disabled: "The Delete project button stays disabled until the name matches exactly."

props.name: loading
props.doc: The action is running. The confirm keeps its label and width, Cancel and Escape are off.

props.name: error
props.doc: The action failed. Shown as an alert above the cost. The dialog stays open and the typed value stays.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The typed value at the start, and after the dialog reopens. Empty by default.

slices.name: destructive-actions
slices.summary: A destructive action removes something. The more it costs, the more the screen should slow you down. A cheap, reversible action should not slow you down at all.

slices.name: disclosure
slices.summary: A disclosure is a heading you can press to show or hide a block of text under it. A group of them stacked together is an accordion, and it can be set so only one stays open.

props.name: title
props.doc: The summary text. It stays visible open or closed.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The content is on its way. The panel shows placeholder lines and sets `aria-busy`.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.doc: Text for assistive technology while loading.

props.name: children
props.doc: The panel.

slices.name: divider
slices.summary: A divider is a thin line that separates two groups of content. It can run across the page or, between items in a row, up and down.

props.name: decorative
props.doc: The line is only decoration. It is then hidden from assistive technology. Default false: the line marks a change of topic.

slices.name: elevation
slices.summary: Elevation says how far a surface floats above the page. A menu floats above a card, and a dialog floats above the menu. The library keeps only two levels, so each one keeps its meaning.

slices.name: empty-results
slices.summary: An empty result is what a list shows when there is nothing to show. It should say why, and give the user a way forward.

slices.name: empty-state
slices.summary: An empty state is what a list or a page shows when there is nothing to show. It says why it is empty, and what to do next.

props.name: title
props.doc: The fact, in a few words: "No projects yet".

props.name: children
props.doc: One or two sentences: why, and what to do.

props.name: media
props.doc: An illustration or an Icon. Hidden from assistive technology: the title says it in words.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The next step: one primary button, and at most one more.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Outline level of the title. Pick it for the page outline; the look does not change. Default 2.

slices.name: filtering
slices.summary: Filtering narrows a long list. It shows what is set, how many results are left, and a way to undo each choice.

slices.name: focus
slices.summary: Focus is the mark that shows which control the keyboard will act on. Without it, keyboard users are lost.

slices.name: form-validation
slices.summary: Form validation is how a form tells you what is wrong and how to fix it. It waits until you finish a field, then says so in plain words next to it.

slices.name: heading
slices.summary: A heading is a title for the part of the page below it. Screen reader users jump from heading to heading to find their way, so the order of the titles matters more than their size.

props.name: level
props.doc: The outline level, 1 to 6. It sets the element (h1 to h6) and nothing about the look.

props.name: size
props.doc: The look. Defaults to the size that suits the level; pass it to look smaller or larger than the outline says.

slices.name: icon
slices.summary: An icon is a small picture that stands for an action or a state, such as a check, a magnifying glass or a warning triangle. It sits beside words or inside a button. It does not replace them.

props.name: glyph
props.doc: The drawing, by name.

props.name: size
props.doc: The side of the icon box, from size.icon.*.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name. Set it only when the icon says something the text nearby does not; without it the icon is hidden from assistive technology.

slices.name: icon-button
slices.summary: An icon button is a button drawn as a small picture, such as a cross to close. Because there is no text, you must give it a name that a screen reader can say.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name. An icon alone names nothing.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon, already sized by its own component. Hidden from assistive technology.

slices.name: iconography
slices.summary: Icons are small pictures for actions and things. They work when they look like one family: the same grid, the same line weight, the same corners. The library draws its own 42, built from circles, squares, triangles and straight lines.

slices.name: link
slices.summary: A link takes you somewhere else: another page, another site, another part of the same page. If pressing it does something in place, like saving, it is a button, not a link.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render, such as an app router's link component. It receives every prop, `href` included. Default: a native `a`.

props.name: external
props.doc: The link leaves the app and opens in a new tab. Adds the icon and the spoken warning.

props.name: externalLabel
props.doc: The warning read out for an external link. Pass it in the app's language.

props.name: current
props.doc: The link points at the place the user is in. Sets `aria-current`; `true` means "page".

props.name: standalone
props.doc: The link stands alone (a nav item, a crumb, a footer link), so it draws at 32px (size.control.md). Leave it off inside a sentence.

slices.name: list
slices.summary: A list is a stack of rows, one thing per row. Each row can have a picture on the left, a name, a line of detail, and a value on the right. A whole row can be one link or one button.

props.name: ordered
props.doc: An `ol` when order carries meaning (a ranking, steps); a `ul` otherwise.

props.name: divided
props.doc: A rule between rows.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Show skeleton rows that mirror the leading, title and description slots.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.doc: Text for assistive technology while loading.

props.name: empty
props.doc: Content when there are no rows. The caller supplies the empty state; the list imports no pattern.

props.name: error
props.doc: The rows failed to load. Replaces the rows; announced as an alert.

props.name: partial
props.doc: Some rows loaded and some did not. Shown under the rows.

props.name: children
props.doc: `ListItem` elements.

slices.name: menu
slices.summary: A menu is a short list of actions that opens from a button. Press the button, pick one action, and the list closes. Arrow keys move, and typing a letter jumps to a match.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The button that opens the menu. It is the tab stop; the menu never takes one. Without it, the open menu is drawn in the flow (a preview or an embedded list): no popover, no focus move.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the menu, usually the trigger's own name.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Which side of the trigger the menu opens on. It flips at the viewport edge.

props.name: portalContainer
props.doc: Mount the open menu in this element instead of the end of the body. For previews and embedded panels.

slices.name: menu-item
slices.summary: A menu item is one row in a menu: an action you can pick. It can carry an icon, a second line of detail and a hint of the keyboard shortcut.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label. A string, so the typeahead and the accessible name have text to use.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A leading glyph. Hidden from assistive technology; the label names the item.

props.name: description
props.doc: A second line under the label, also read as the item's description.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: A hint of the key combination, such as "Ctrl+S". A hint only; the app binds the key.

props.name: destructive
props.doc: The item deletes or discards something. It reads in the error colour, and its label must say what it deletes.

slices.name: messaging
slices.summary: Messaging is how the product tells a user something. Most of the time the best message is none. When one is needed, pick the one that interrupts least.

slices.name: modal
slices.summary: A modal is a small window that stops you and asks for a few details. You finish the task or close it, and then you are back where you were.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the dialog is shown. The parent owns this state.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on Escape, on a scrim click (when allowed), and on the close button. Set `open` to false in response.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the dialog. It labels the dialog and is the fallback focus target.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The actions row. It stays in view while the body scrolls.

props.name: size
props.doc: Maximum inline size, from size.overlay.*.

props.name: role
props.doc: `alertdialog` for a message that needs a response. AlertDialog and ConfirmationDialog set it.

props.name: dismissOnScrim
props.doc: Close on a click on the scrim. Off by default, so a stray click never loses typed work.

props.name: closeLabel
props.doc: The accessible name of the close button. Without it, no close button is drawn.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Content is loading. The body is marked aria-busy.

props.name: inline
props.doc: Render open, in the flow, with no scrim and no focus trap. For previews and embedded panels.

slices.name: motion
slices.summary: Motion is how things move between states. Small, quick movement tells users something changed. Long or looping movement gets in the way.

slices.name: pagination
slices.summary: Pagination cuts a long list into pages and lets you move between them, like the page numbers at the bottom of a search result.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the landmark, such as "Pagination".

props.name: page
props.doc: The current page, from 1.

props.name: onPageChange
props.doc: Called with the new page. In link mode it runs on click too, for a client-side route change.

props.name: getHref
props.doc: Link mode: each page is a link to this URL, so back, reload and sharing work. Without it, each page is a button.

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: A router link component for link mode, rendered instead of `a`.

props.name: total
props.doc: The range and count as text, already formatted: "1–25 of 1,342".

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: The page-size select.

props.name: pageLabel
props.doc: The accessible name of a page item. Default: "Page n".

props.name: status
props.doc: Announced when the page changes, such as "Page 3 of 60". Renders a polite live region.

props.name: siblings
props.doc: How many pages show on each side of the current one. Default 1.

props.name: pageClassName
props.doc: An extra class on one page control, for a forced state in a showcase.

slices.name: popover
slices.summary: A popover is a small panel that appears next to the button you pressed. It holds a bit more than a hint: a few options, a short form, some detail. Press outside or Escape and it goes away.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The button that opens the popover. Without it, the open popover is drawn in the flow (a preview or an embedded panel): no anchoring, no focus move.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the popover content.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content. A function receives `close`, for an action inside the popover.

props.name: modal
props.doc: Modal: the page behind is inert and an outside press closes it. Non-modal (default): the page stays reachable, and moving focus away closes it.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Which side of the trigger the popover opens on. It flips at the viewport edge.

props.name: portalContainer
props.doc: Mount the open popover in this element instead of the end of the body. For previews and embedded panels.

slices.name: progress
slices.summary: A progress bar shows how far a long task has got, such as an upload. It always says what it is and how much is done, in words as well as in the bar.

props.name: label
props.doc: The visible label: what is in progress, such as "Uploading report.pdf".

props.name: value
props.doc: How much is done. Leave it out for an indeterminate bar (unknown length).

props.name: max
props.doc: The value that means done. Default 100.

props.name: valueText
props.doc: The value in words, shown beside the label. Defaults to the percent. Also the accessible value text.

props.name: error
props.doc: The work failed. Shown as text with an icon; the bar takes the error colour.

slices.name: radio-group
slices.summary: A radio group is a short list where you choose exactly one, and every choice is visible. Picking one un-picks the other. A question above the list says what you are choosing.

props.name: legend
props.doc: The question the options answer. It becomes the legend, so a screen reader announces it with each option.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text. Its presence sets aria-invalid on the group.

props.name: name
props.doc: Shared by the radios. It makes them one group with one Tab stop. A generated name is used when omitted.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Uncontrolled starting value. Preselect only with a reason: a chosen default hides the question.

props.name: onBlur
props.doc: Group blur: called when focus leaves the group, not when it moves from one radio to another. Validate here.

slices.name: saving
slices.summary: Saving should never be a guess. The page tells you, in one fixed place, whether your work is safe: not yet, in progress, saved, or lost and what to do.

slices.name: select
slices.summary: A select is a drop-down list. You pick one item from a short list of choices that are already known: a country, a size, a status.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text. Its presence sets aria-invalid and the error look.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.doc: Text of the empty choice, such as "Choose a country". Leave it out when a value is always preselected.

props.name: readOnly
props.doc: The value shows but cannot change. A native select has no readonly attribute, so this blocks the opening keys and clicks.

slices.name: shape
slices.summary: Shape is how round the corners are. Sharp corners feel strict, round ones feel friendly. The library picks one for controls and keeps it.

slices.name: skeleton
slices.summary: A skeleton is a grey outline of what is about to appear. It holds the space while content loads, so the page does not jump when the content arrives.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The placeholder shape: a line of text, a rectangle, or a circle. Mirror the real layout.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines of text. Only for `shape="text"`. The last line is shorter.

props.name: width
props.doc: CSS inline size, as a token expression such as `var(--ds-space-12)`.

props.name: height
props.doc: CSS block size, as a token expression.

slices.name: spacing
slices.summary: Spacing is the air between things. Close things read as one group. Far things read as separate. One fixed set of gaps keeps every screen in the same rhythm.

slices.name: spinner
slices.summary: A spinner is a small turning ring that says 'working on it'. Use it for a short wait of one or two seconds, in the spot where the result will appear.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name, such as "Loading orders". Say what loads.

props.name: size
props.doc: The side of the ring, from size.icon.*.

props.name: showLabel
props.doc: Show the label beside the ring instead of hiding it from sight.

slices.name: stack
slices.summary: A stack puts things in a line, one after the other, with an even gap between them. The line runs down the page or across it.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Use "ul" or "ol" with `li` children for a list: the stack resets its markers and padding, and keeps the list role.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap between children, as a space step.

props.name: align
props.doc: Alignment on the cross axis.

props.name: justify
props.doc: Distribution on the main axis.

props.name: wrap
props.doc: Let children flow onto a new line instead of shrinking or overflowing.

slices.name: switch
slices.summary: A switch is a light switch on screen. Flip it and the setting changes at once: notifications on, dark mode off. There is no Save button.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the setting. It never changes with the state: "Email alerts", not "Email alerts on".

slices.name: table
slices.summary: A table lays rows of facts along shared columns, so you can scan down a column and compare. Use it when people look up exact values, sort them and pick some. When each row holds one thing, use a list.

props.name: caption
props.doc: The table's name. Required: it names the table and its scroll region.

props.name: hideCaption
props.doc: Keep the caption for assistive technology and hide it from the eye.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.doc: The name of a row's checkbox, such as its identifier. Defaults to the row id.

props.name: sort
props.doc: The column and direction the caller has sorted by.

props.name: selectedIds
props.doc: Ids of the selected rows, on any page. Giving `onSelectionChange` turns on the checkbox column.

props.name: sticky
props.doc: Keep the header in view. Give the root a `max-block-size` so the region scrolls.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Show skeleton rows that mirror the columns.

props.name: empty
props.doc: Content for a row set with no rows. The caller supplies the empty state; the table imports no pattern.

props.name: error
props.doc: The rows failed to load. Replaces the rows; announced as an alert.

props.name: partial
props.doc: Some rows loaded and some did not. Shown under the rows.

slices.name: tabs
slices.summary: Tabs let you flip between a few views of the same thing without leaving the page, like the tabs of a folder. Only one view shows at a time.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the tab list.

props.name: value
props.doc: The selected tab id, for a controlled tabs.

props.name: activation
props.doc: "automatic" selects a tab when it takes focus. "manual" waits for Enter or Space.

slices.name: text
slices.summary: Text is how words appear on screen. It picks the size and the weight so that a heading looks like a heading and a note looks like a note.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Pick it for document structure; the variant only sets the look.

slices.name: text-field
slices.summary: A text field is a box where you type one line: your name, an email address, a search. A label above it says what to type. If something goes wrong, a message under it says what and how to fix it.

props.name: label
props.doc: Always visible. A placeholder is never the label (WCAG 3.3.2).

props.name: description
props.doc: Help shown between the label and the input, tied with aria-describedby.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text. Its presence sets aria-invalid and the error look. Say what is wrong and how to fix it.

props.name: success
props.doc: A quiet confirmation, such as "Meets the 12 character rule". Announced politely, styled as success, never as an error. Hidden while `error` is set.

props.name: requiredText
props.doc: The word that explains the required marker. Default "required".

props.name: errorPrefix
props.doc: The hidden word before the error text. Default "Error".

props.name: successPrefix
props.doc: The hidden word before the success text. Default "Correct".

props.name: type
props.doc: Pick the type that matches the data, so the keyboard and validation fit.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: Show a clear button while the field holds text. On by default for `type="search"`.

props.name: clearLabel
props.doc: The name of the clear button. Default "Clear search" for a search field, else "Clear".

props.name: onClear
props.doc: Called after the clear button emptied the field and returned focus to it.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: Content inside the box, after the text: a unit, an icon, a small button. Give a button its own accessible name.

slices.name: textarea
slices.summary: A textarea is a text field with room for several lines: a message, a comment, an address. It grows with what you write and you can drag its corner to make it taller.

props.name: label
props.doc: Always visible. A placeholder is never the label (WCAG 3.3.2).

props.name: error
props.doc: The error text. Its presence sets aria-invalid and the error look.

props.name: count
props.doc: The text shows "n / max" when both `maxLength` and a count are known. Pass the current length.

slices.name: toast
slices.summary: A toast is a small message that slides in to say that something happened, such as 'Draft saved', and goes away by itself. It never grabs your keyboard focus.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of each close button.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Default time on screen, in ms. Default 5000.

props.name: max
props.doc: Most toasts shown at once. The rest wait, and show as the first ones close. Default 3.

props.name: moreLabel
props.doc: Text for the waiting toasts, such as "+2 more".

props.name: position
props.doc: `fixed` sits at the corner of the viewport, `static` stays in the flow (for a specimen).

slices.name: tooltip
slices.summary: A tooltip is a few words that pop up when you point at a button or tab to it. It adds a detail to something that already has a name. It never holds anything you have to do.

props.name: children
props.doc: The control the tooltip describes. It must already have its own name.

props.name: content
props.doc: A short hint. A string, so it can never hold a link or a button.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Which side of the trigger the tooltip opens on. It flips at the viewport edge.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Milliseconds of hover or focus before it opens.

props.name: portalContainer
props.doc: Mount the open tooltip in this element instead of the end of the body. For previews and embedded panels.

slices.name: typography
slices.summary: Typography is how words look: which typeface, how big, how heavy, how tall each line is. Typefaces are the fonts you own, fonts are the jobs, and text styles are how a job looks at each size. A heading looks the same wherever it appears.

slices.name: visually-hidden
slices.summary: Some text is for screen readers only, such as 'opens in a new tab' or 'Close' next to an icon. Visually hidden keeps that text out of sight and in the page for assistive technology.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Use "a" with `focusable` for a skip link.

props.name: focusable
props.doc: Appear on keyboard focus. For a skip link and any control that must be reachable but not always seen.

props.name: href
props.doc: The target, when `as` is "a".
